suggestions: filter store_returns early with date bounds
use EXISTS for filtering catalog sales
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
split a complex join into multiple CTEs
optimized_sql:
WITH date_bounds AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT
        (SELECT MIN(d_date_sk) FROM date_dim WHERE d_year = 1999 AND d_moy = 4) AS d1_min,
        (SELECT MAX(d_date_sk) FROM date_dim WHERE d_year = 1999 AND d_moy = 4) AS d1_max,
        (SELECT MIN(d_date_sk) FROM date_dim WHERE d_year = 1999 AND d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10) AS d23_min,
        (SELECT MAX(d_date_sk) FROM date_dim WHERE d_year = 1999 AND d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10) AS d23_max
),
store_returns_filtered AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT sr.sr_customer_sk,
           sr.sr_item_sk,
           sr.sr_ticket_number,
           sr.sr_net_loss
    FROM store_returns sr
    WHERE sr.sr_returned_date_sk BETWEEN (SELECT d23_min FROM date_bounds) AND (SELECT d23_max FROM date_bounds)
),
sr_sales_probe AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT sr.sr_customer_sk,
           sr.sr_item_sk,
           sales_probe.ss_store_sk,
           MAX(sales_probe.ss_net_profit) AS ss_net_profit,
           MAX(sr.sr_net_loss) AS sr_net_loss
    FROM store_returns_filtered sr
    JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT ss.ss_store_sk,
               ss.ss_net_profit
        FROM store_sales ss
        WHERE ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
          AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
          AND ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
          AND ss.ss_sold_date_sk BETWEEN (SELECT d1_min FROM date_bounds) AND (SELECT d1_max FROM date_bounds)
    ) sales_probe ON TRUE
    GROUP BY sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_item_sk, sales_probe.ss_store_sk
),
catalog_agg AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT cs.cs_bill_customer_sk,
           cs.cs_item_sk,
           MAX(cs.cs_net_profit) AS cs_net_profit
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    WHERE cs.cs_sold_date_sk BETWEEN (SELECT d23_min FROM date_bounds) AND (SELECT d23_max FROM date_bounds)
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM sr_sales_probe p
          WHERE p.sr_customer_sk = cs.cs_bill_customer_sk
            AND p.sr_item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
      )
    GROUP BY cs.cs_bill_customer_sk, cs.cs_item_sk
)
SELECT i.i_item_id,
       i.i_item_desc,
       s.s_store_id,
       s.s_store_name,
       MAX(sa.ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
       MAX(sa.sr_net_loss) AS store_returns_loss,
       MAX(ca.cs_net_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM sr_sales_probe sa
JOIN catalog_agg ca
  ON ca.cs_bill_customer_sk = sa.sr_customer_sk
 AND ca.cs_item_sk = sa.sr_item_sk
JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = sa.sr_item_sk
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_store_sk = sa.ss_store_sk
GROUP BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
LIMIT 100

1. LATERAL PK PROBE — TARGET: `store_sales` joined to `store_returns` on `(sr_ticket_number, sr_item_sk, sr_customer_sk)` — TRANSFORMATION: Drive from d2-filtered `store_returns` and probe the single `store_sales` row by its primary key `(ss_ticket_number, ss_item_sk)`, applying `ss_customer_sk` and the d1 April-1999 date check as residual predicates; add a covering index on `store_sales(ss_ticket_number, ss_item_sk)` including `ss_sold_date_sk, ss_customer_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_net_profit` so the 57M-row `store_sales` table is not hash-scanned.

2. PRE-AGGREGATE RETURN/SALE MATCHES — TARGET: the joined `store_returns ⋈ store_sales` rows — TRANSFORMATION: Before touching `catalog_sales`, group the surviving matches by `(sr_customer_sk, sr_item_sk, ss_store_sk)` with `MAX(ss_net_profit)` and `MAX(sr_net_loss)`, collapsing multiple tickets/return rows into one row per relevant key combination.

3. SEMI-JOIN-REDUCED CATALOG MAX — TARGET: `catalog_sales` grouped by `(cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_item_sk)` — TRANSFORMATION: Extract the distinct `(customer, item)` key set from the step-2 aggregate, semi-join `catalog_sales` to that set with the d3 1999 Apr–Oct date condition, then compute `MAX(cs_net_profit)` per `(customer, item)`; this avoids aggregating catalog rows that can never match the final result.

4. DATE_DIM RANGE BOUNDS — TARGET: `date_dim d1/d2/d3` joins on `ss_sold_date_sk`, `sr_returned_date_sk`, `cs_sold_date_sk` — TRANSFORMATION: Collapse the `d_year`/`d_moy` predicates into `d_date_sk` range bounds computed once from `date_dim`, and apply those ranges directly to the three fact tables, so `date_dim` rows do not participate in the large hash joins.

5. COVERING CATALOG INDEX — TARGET: `catalog_sales(cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_item_sk)` — TRANSFORMATION: Add a covering index on those keys including `cs_sold_date_sk` and `cs_net_profit`, enabling the step-3 semi-join/aggregate to be an index-only operation rather than a full 28.8M-row scan/group.
